## TL;DR

Replaced the muted surface token used as text color in Pipeline cards and model test summaries with the semantic secondary-text token `--txt-dim`. Extended the stylesheet source guard so a future `color: var(--muted)` declaration is reported, while muted backgrounds remain valid. Added dark and light Pipeline review shots for the card text.

## Work and rationale

The reported issue came from a semantic mismatch in the theme palette. `--muted` represents a low-emphasis surface and tracks the surrounding panel in both light and dark appearances. It is intentionally useful for backgrounds, but makes foreground text blend into the card. `--txt-dim` already expresses the desired hierarchy: quieter than primary text while remaining legible, with theme-specific values supplied by the existing theme blocks.

Updated the task id, type and priority chips, elapsed-time label, and model/host metadata row in `PipelineCard.vue`. These are the secondary labels named in the report; title, stage, and status text retain their existing foreground or status colors. A repository-wide search of the UI source found no remaining `color: var(--muted)` declarations. The remaining `--muted` references are a token alias and background tint calculations, so the surface token itself remains unchanged.

Applied the same correction to `.model-test-summary` and `.model-test-not_testable` in the global stylesheet. This covers the two adjacent instances called out in the task and avoids leaving the same semantic bug elsewhere.

The existing hard-coded-color source guard now classifies `color: var(--muted)` as an offender, and its unit test verifies both sides of the distinction: text color is rejected, but `background: var(--muted)` is accepted. This keeps the guard focused on misuse as foreground text rather than banning legitimate surface styling. The repo dogfood test scans the configured UI source roots, so the rule applies across scoped component styles and the global stylesheet.

Declared the requested `/work` Pipeline captures using the `pipeline:checksProgress` fixture in dark and light themes. Each shot highlights a pipeline card and asserts that the task id and model/host row are present for review.

## Approaches tried

The task called for changing the call sites rather than redefining `--muted`; the code follows that boundary. `--txt-dim` was chosen because it is already the canonical secondary text token used around the affected UI. I retained the current card structure and typography so the fix changes legibility without altering layout or the board view.

For regression protection, I extended the existing source guard rather than creating a separate CSS-specific test mechanism. The guard already parses style blocks and reports source locations. Adding the semantic check there means new misuse is caught by the configured check, and the unit test documents why a muted background is still allowed.

## Challenges and blockers

The task’s requested screenshot metadata was set through `repoos update`, as required by the repository workflow. The CLI noted that this session is inside a linked worktree and reads the main checkout’s board for task metadata; no source files outside this worktree were read or edited as part of the implementation. The worktree task copy remains the specification and is not hand-edited.

No visual browser session was launched. The task provides declared shots as its review evidence path, and RepoOS captures those during handoff. The scoped RepoOS check is the verification gate for this session; its result is recorded by the check itself rather than inferred here.

## Key learnings

Theme token names can be misleading when a shadcn-style `muted` token is used without distinguishing its surface role from muted foreground text. Semantic text tokens should be used for all secondary labels, while surface tokens belong in backgrounds and tints. The source guard now enforces that distinction at the declaration level and still permits intended surface uses.
